bun test >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; git stash -u >/dev/null && bun test 2>&1 | grep -c "Unhandled exception"; git stash pop

result: `GET /health` now runs a real dependency check on every probe. I added `app/Health/DatabaseHealthCheck.ts`, a `HealthCheck` (from the framework's health module, re-exported by `@guren/core`) that resolves the app's Drizzle handle via `getDatabase()` and executes `select 1` on each call — nothing cached — catching both a query failure and a connection that cannot be opened; its connector is constructor-injectable so failure paths are unit-testable. `app/Health/index.ts` wires that check into a `HealthManager` as `critical` with a 2s timeout (critical matters: a non-critical failure would only downgrade the report to `degraded`, which still answers 200) and exposes `healthStatusCode()`, which maps `unhealthy → 503` and everything else to 200. `app/Http/Controllers/HealthController.ts` runs the manager per request and returns `{ status, timestamp, checks: [{ name: "database", status, message, duration }] }` with that status code, and `routes/web.ts` points the still-unnamed, still-exempt `/health` route at it (no route name, so `.guren/routes.gen.ts` is unchanged). `config/database.ts` gained an exported `AppDatabase` type so the raw-SQL cast is named where the dialect is chosen. `tests/HealthController.test.ts` covers the 200/healthy HTTP path plus unhealthy results for a refused connection and a throwing query, and the report-to-503 mapping; `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (8 tests) both pass, and I separately verified end-to-end in a throwaway test that pointing the resolver at an unopenable file turns the probe into `503 {"status":"unhealthy", checks:[{name:"database",status:"unhealthy","message":"unable to open database file"}]}`.
